subject: Add a 1.4 gate to MPI-450: stable is wrapper 0.2.40, so shipping H3 today means a 10-hour download for every user
body:
ACTION: add one gate to MPI-450, because my session is closing and MPI-491 will otherwise sit in doing/validating as a card nobody re-reads. I am not editing MPI-450 myself - it is not my card - so this is the request.

GATE TO ADD: 'Promote the Pod runtime dev -> stable (publish-runtime.sh promote) before cutting 1.4.0. Blocked on the GPU-image _download_hf measurement (MPI-491 / MPI-467).'

WHY THIS IS A RELEASE GATE AND NOT CLEANUP. I checked both halves just now:
  - MiniMax H3 and MiniMax H3 Reference are HEADLINE items in docs/releases/UNRELEASED.md (lines 123 and 135).
  - https://pod.cubric.studio/vision/stable/manifest.json today reports wrapper_version 0.2.40.
  - Released builds only ever boot the stable channel; only a dev app run boots dev (MPI-340, CLAUDE.md context router).
Put together: if 1.4.0 ships while stable is 0.2.40, every released user who installs H3 onto a Pod gets the aria2 path at 1.66 MB/s. That is about 10 hours for the ~46GB H3 set, on a headline feature of the biggest release since 1.0. The measured alternative is ~2.5 minutes. Nobody would report it as a bug - it just looks like H3 is enormous.

SCOPE, so the gate is not written wider than the evidence:
  - REMOTE/Pod installs only. The local engine is unaffected and needs no change: from a home line HF serves 43.9 MB/s and R2 47.0, so the last mile is the cap. A local H3 install is roughly 30 minutes at that speed, which is also the honest number if the release notes ever quote one.
  - It affects the six huggingface.co deps only. The 101 R2 and 14 github deps are unchanged and still on aria2.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS for whoever clears it: your controlnet-union-flux number on the GPU image first, then promote, then cut. Promoting before that measurement puts an unmeasured transport in front of every released user, which is the one thing publish-runtime.sh warns about in its own output.

SECOND ITEM, lower priority, same reason - it will otherwise be lost. The Dockerfile RIFE prebake still points at huggingface.co on the strength of a claim that is now false. docs/runpod-troubleshooting.md said marduk191/rife was 'a plain non-Xet repo, never 403s'; I verified 2026-08-08 that it 302s to us.aws.cdn.hf.co/xet-bridge-us like everything else, and MPI-148 is on record that this CDN 403s ranged aria2 non-deterministically and broke the whole docker build. Doc is corrected (9be9dfc3) but the Dockerfile is not. It is an image-build flake risk, not a user-facing one, so it does not gate 1.4 - it just needs a card before it bites a build at a bad moment.
resolution: Resolved 2026-08-10 by mpi-cleanup, on the user's call: leftovers, nobody is using them. The whole thread ran MPI-491 -> MPI-467 and BOTH cards are now done/complete. The one action aimed at a live card (af21aa8f, add a 1.4 gate to MPI-450) was WITHDRAWN by 9805e50a in the same thread, because mpi-release already stops on the manifest diff. Nothing here is outstanding.
